title: ‘Devil’ ringleader who tortured, killed transgender man Sam Nordquist held captive in NY motel sentenced to life in prison
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The devilish ringleader who helped torture and murder a transgender man at an upstate New York motel was handed the maximum punishment on Tuesday as the courtroom erupted in cheers.

Precious Arzuaga and her ex-girlfriend Jennifer Quijano were sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for their roles in the deadly month-long torture of Sam Nordquist in 2025.

“F–k you. You’re the devil,” a spectator inside the Ontario County court gallery shouted as others praised Judge Kristina Karle’s heavy punishment, according to the Times Union.

Arzuaga, who pleaded guilty to first-degree murder in July, kept her head hung to the ground, only lifting it to blow a kiss to her mother as she was escorted out of the room.

“We all want to know why,” Karle asked. “Why was someone so good taken so tragically? Was it because Sam was everything you were not and will never be?

Nordquist, a 24-year-old transgender man, was found dead in a field in Yates County on Feb. 13, 2025.

The Minnesota transplant had been staying with Arzuaga at Patty’s Lodge motel in Canandaigua, roughly 30 minutes outside of Rochester, since he arrived in the Empire State in September 2024.

Arzuaga lured Nordquist to the region under the prospect of a loving relationship but instead began a campaign of torment stretching from Jan. 1, 2025 to Feb. 2, 2025.

“Sadly and tragically, he found you. And you represent everything opposite of Sam,” Karle said.

The devious woman led a group of six others, including Quijano and two children — one of whom was her son — to beat, torture and sexually assault Nordquist inside the motel room.

Nordquist was punched, kicked, beaten with sticks, dog toys, ropes canes and belts — and assaulted with a table leg and broomstick in the weeks leading to his death.

He died of repeated acts of violence and torture, authorities ruled.

Nordquist was reported missing by family members on Feb. 9, after he lost contact with them.

He was found dumped in the field in Yates County wrapped in plastic several days later.

For the grueling month, Nordquist was held captive inside and caged like a dog in a cynical crime prosecutors compared to a Hollywood horror film.

“This is the worst of the worst,” Ontario County First Assistant District Attorney James Nobles said. “It may be common on television or in the movies, but not in real life.”

Nordquist’s mother and sister spoke before Arzuaga was sentenced.

“Sam had the gentlest heart of anyone I’ve ever known,” his mother Linda said. “He saw the good in people. Even when they did not deserve it.”

Prosecutors didn’t disclose a motive for Arzuaga’s actions but revealed chilling text messages she had sent before Nordquist’s murder.

“Sam can never leave New York alive,” one message from Arzuaga read, as attorneys characterized it as “torture for torture sake,” WHAM reported.

Both Arzuaga and Quijano pleaded guilty in July to all charges they faced, including first-degree murder, kidnapping, conspiracy, aggravated sexual abuse, concealment of a human corpse and endangering the welfare of a child.

Quijano’s involvement in Nordquist’s torture and murder was motivated by jealousy after Arzuaga’s attention was no longer focused on her, prosecutors said.

“It’s just that Sam had Precious’s attention and she hated him for it,” Assistant District Attorney Sara Van Strydonck said. “So you want to know the motive? The motive is jealousy.”

Emily Motyka and Kyle Sage both pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and second-degree kidnapping for their roles in Nordquist’s death. They are awaiting sentencing.

The three remaining defendants — including Patrick Goodwin and Thomas Eaves — are scheduled to go to trial in January.
